newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian on trial next week for Israeli killings.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian on trial next week for Israeli killings.

text.p: A military court outside Amman will put on trial a Jordanian soldier next week for the premeditated murder of seven Israeli schoolgirls, the soldier's defence lawyer said on Wednesday.
Ahmed Nijdawi said his client, Ahmed al-Daqamsa, faced death by hanging if found guilty by the five-member panel of military judges, led by Brigadier Mamoun Khasawneh.
The trial was expected to open on Tuesday at a military court near Naour, a few miles south of Amman, the lawyer said.
Witnesses said Daqamsa opened fire on the girls while they were on school outing last March to a piece of Jordanian farmland leased to Israel under a 1994 peace treaty.
Nijdawi said his client had not denied the shooting, but said he acted on the spur of the moment when the girls teased him. He said Daqamsa also justified it as a "nationalist" act.
"He is in good condition. There are no problems for him," Nijdawi told Reuters. "He is a faithful man."
Jordanian newspapers said Nijdawi would also face a charge of military mutiny.
